title: Error Response Format
description: Design a consistent, machine-readable error response format that includes error codes, field-level details, and documentation links.

data.text: A consistent error response format lets clients handle failures programmatically. Every error should include a machine-readable code, a human-readable message, a unique request ID for support, and a documentation URL.
Follow RFC 7807 (Problem Details) or extend it with additional fields for better developer experience.

data.title: RFC 7807-compatible error response
data.content: Minimal standard format with custom extensions.
data.code:
{
  "type": "https://api.example.com/errors/validation-failed",
  "title": "Validation Failed",
  "status": 422,
  "detail": "The request body contains invalid fields.",
  "instance": "/users",
  "requestId": "req_abc123",
  "timestamp": "2026-10-06T15:30:00Z",
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "email",
      "issue": "Must be a valid email address",
      "value": "not-an-email"
    }
  ],
  "documentationUrl": "https://docs.example.com/errors/validation-failed"
}

data.text: Validation errors must tell the client exactly which field failed and why. A generic 'validation failed' message forces clients to inspect the entire request body.

data.title: 422 with field-level validation errors
data.content: Each error entry names the field, the specific issue, and the received value.

data.text: Centralize error formatting in a global exception handler so every endpoint returns the same structure automatically.

data.title: Global error handler in Express.js
data.content: Middleware that intercepts all errors and formats them consistently.

data.title: Include a request ID
data.text: Every error response must include a unique request ID. Clients include this ID in support tickets. You use it to look up the exact server-side log entry without asking the client for timing, IP, or request details.

items.question: Should I include the stack trace in error responses?
items.answer: Never in production. Stack traces leak internal class names, file paths, and dependency versions. Log them server-side with the request ID and return only the error code and message.

items.question: How do I handle errors from downstream services?
items.answer: Map downstream errors to your own error codes. Do not expose internal service names or error messages. Return 502 Bad Gateway or 504 Gateway Timeout with your own error format.

items.question: Should error codes be stable or can they change?
items.answer: Error codes are part of your API contract. Once published, never change or remove them. You can add new codes, but existing ones must remain forever.

data.title: Key takeaway
points: Use RFC 7807 as the base and extend with requestId and documentationUrl.
Validation errors must include field-level detail.
Never expose stack traces or internal service names.
Error codes are stable API contracts.
data.takeaway: Error responses are the API contract when things go wrong. Make them as machine-readable and actionable as your success responses.
